newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-Dutch PTT higher 1996 profit, sees 1997 rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dutch PTT higher 1996 profit, sees 1997 rise.

text.p: Dutch post and telecoms group Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN) on Tuesday posted a rise in 1996 net profits of over nine percent and said it saw further profit growth in 1997.

Net profit rose 9.1 percent to 2.46 billion guilders ($1.3 billion) from 2.26 billlion, with the dividend climbing to 2.85 guilders per share from 2.60 guilders. Sales increased 10.6 percent to 21.33 billion guilders.

"For 1997, KPN expects a substantial growth of turnover and a clear growth of the profit after taxes," the company said in a statement with the results, which were bang in line with analysts' forecasts for an 8-10 percent rise in net.
"KPN also bases its expectations on a strong growth of the market for mobile telecommunications and a continuing growth of demand for newly introduced and existing services," it said.
But steady growth in sales would be accompanied by continuing pressure on prices, KPN added in a statement.
Structural factors which led to lower telecommunication tariffs in 1996 are seen continuing unabated in 1997 but measures taken by KPN to contain costs will also be maintained.
"Our (profit) expectation does not take into account the possible effects on the profit after taxes of further acquisitions or divestments in 1997," KPN said.
It added that it expected to double turnover from postal activities, partly as a result of the recent takeover of Australian transport and express delivery service TNT TNT.AX.

Part of the reasoning behind the TNT acquisition was to create a balance between revenues from the postal and telecoms units which turned over 6.71 billion guilders and 14.28 billion guilders respectively in 1996.
Investments in acquisitions and fixed assets mushroomed 78 percent to 8.72 billion guilders in 1996, the group said.

This was due both to high profile buys such as the takeover of Australia's TNT by PTT Post and the acquisition of key minority shareholdings in Telecom Eireann of Ireland and PT Telkomsel of Indonesia.
New takeovers were possible in the current year and KPN said it was keeping open the option of raising additional funds on the capital market in the course of 1997.
KPN chairman Wim Dik told reporters the performance seen during 1996 pointed to reliable growth. "All business units contributed to that result which is very satisfying," he said.
PTT Post booked 1996 sales growth of 10.4 percent from 6.08 billion guilders, with more than half the growth coming from acquisitions and takeovers during the year.
Belgian distribution service Belgische Distributiedienst NV, night distribution company NET and Bruna and De Boekelier bookshops all contributed, the company said.
PTT telecom increased sales by 9.3 percent, mainly due to a rise in national telephony and mobile telecoms sales.

Within the unit national telephony sales increased mostly through telephony and partly through higher directories sales. International telephony sales decreased by 7.2 percent, however, with a seven percent volume growth not enough to offset negative price and foreign exchange effects.
Dik told reporters the company was still mulling separate listings for its post and telecoms arms, adding he did not wish to speculate on the possible outcome.

"Should this lead to a total split up is a question which should be looked into very thoroughly. We have to find an answer to this strategic question first internally and then externally. We think that in the second half of the year we will have found that answer," Dik told reporters.
Most analysts were sticking to current forecasts following the result.
"The figures and forecast are in line with expectations and the dividend of 2.85 guilders per share was just below our estimate," said NIBStrating Securities analyst Rene Verhoef.
Analysts said the company might start to feel the force of competitive pressure in the increasingly deregulated telecommunications market during the current year.

"KPN forecasts more growth for 1997 which is good, but it would be interesting to hear how they intend to boost sales... as competition will become harder as new competitors enter the (Dutch) market," said Steven Vrolijk of ING Barings.
KPN shares closed down 0.80 guilders at 69.40 guilders on profit-taking following Monday's 3.10 guilder rise in anticipation of the results.
($ = 1.919 Dutch Guilders)
